description: Earth’s surface is constantly shifting. NISAR Earth Change Monitor transforms NASA satellite data into actionable insights. We’re building an interactive web app where users can select any region, compare SAR observations over time, and visualize changes from earthquakes, landslides, wildfires, agriculture, and glaciers—showing where, how much, and when change occurs. Seeking teammates in Web Dev, GIS, AI, and Design!
summary:
**NISAR Earth Intelligence – Satellite-Based Earth Change Monitoring**

NISAR Earth Intelligence is a web-based platform designed to monitor and analyze changes on Earth's surface using satellite imagery and geospatial data. It helps users identify where environmental changes occur, estimate their extent, track when they happen, and understand their possible nature.

The platform allows users to select an area of interest, explore available satellite data, and compare observations across different time periods. It currently uses Sentinel-2 imagery and spectral indices such as NDVI for vegetation monitoring and NDWI for water and flood detection. It also integrates NASA data discovery services to explore NISAR satellite observations, alongside interactive maps and AI-assisted explanations of analysis results.

By transforming complex satellite data into accessible visual insights, the platform supports faster environmental assessment and informed decision-making. It is important because monitoring floods, vegetation changes, and other environmental conditions can help communities, researchers, and decision-makers better understand risks, prioritize field inspections, and support more effective environmental management.
details:
Project Details – NISAR Earth Intelligence

NISAR Earth Intelligence is a web-based satellite monitoring platform that helps users detect, explore, and understand changes occurring on Earth's surface. It is designed to make satellite-based environmental monitoring more accessible by transforming complex geospatial data into clear visual information and actionable insights.

How It Works

Users begin by selecting an area of interest on an interactive map and choosing two time periods for comparison. The platform searches for available satellite observations and displays relevant data coverage. It integrates NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR) to explore available NISAR satellite observations and uses Sentinel-2 imagery for its current environmental change analysis.

The platform applies spectral indices to identify specific environmental conditions:

  • NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index): Helps identify vegetation conditions and changes.
  • NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index): Helps identify water-related changes and potential flood areas.

The results are presented through interactive maps, visual comparisons, and analytical indicators. An AI-assisted feature helps users interpret the results in understandable language, while a report-generation feature allows them to save their findings as PDF reports.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to reduce the complexity of accessing and interpreting satellite data. It can support researchers, environmental organizations, students, and decision-makers in monitoring vegetation changes, identifying potential flood-affected areas, and prioritizing locations for further field inspection. By providing accessible visual insights, it encourages data-driven environmental assessment and can contribute to better planning and resource management.

Technologies and Tools

We developed the platform using:

  • HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for the user interface and interactive functionality.
  • Python for supporting data-processing tasks.
  • SciPy for scientific and numerical processing.
  • NASA CMR for discovering satellite observations.
  • Sentinel-2 satellite imagery for vegetation and water analysis.
  • OpenStreetMap for geographic visualization and mapping.
  • Google's Gemini API for AI-assisted explanations.

The project is software-based and does not require specialized hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of our project is the integration of satellite data discovery, environmental analysis, interactive geographic visualization, and AI-assisted interpretation into one platform. Instead of simply displaying satellite images, it helps users investigate where changes may have occurred, estimate their extent, compare different periods, and understand their possible environmental significance.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered data availability, geographic coverage, processing complexity, usability, clarity of results, and the importance of presenting reliable information. We also considered the limitations of satellite observations and the need to distinguish between detected indicators and confirmed real-world damage. NISAR data discovery is integrated into the platform, while the current vegetation and water analysis is based on Sentinel-2 imagery, leaving room for future integration of direct NISAR radar-based change analysis.
